proximal_attachment.landmark: diaphragmatic muscular fibers converging from the sternal, costal, and lumbar (crural) parts

distal_attachment.landmark: no bony insertion -- the muscular fibers converge onto and terminate within this fibrous central sheet itself, which then attaches to the pericardium above rather than to bone

parts.name: Central tendon
parts.function_note: A trefoil (clover-leaf)-shaped, largely non-elastic fibrous sheet into which all three muscular parts of the diaphragm (sternal, costal, lumbar/crural) converge and insert; unlike most named tendons it has no direct bony attachment of its own -- it is fused superiorly to the fibrous pericardium, and its relative fixity (compared to the surrounding muscular diaphragm) is what allows diaphragmatic contraction to actually descend/flatten the dome during inspiration rather than simply shortening in place.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)
parts.attachment_or_location: apex of the diaphragmatic dome, fused to the pericardium

function: The diaphragm's central fibrous sheet -- structurally a tendon (all diaphragmatic muscle fibers insert into it) but functionally unusual in having a fibrous, not bony, distal partner (the pericardium), and in being the fixed point around which the entire muscle's contraction is organized.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

proximal_attachment.landmark: internal oblique + transversus abdominis muscle bellies (representative, lower fibers)

parts.name: Conjoint tendon
parts.function_note: The fused aponeurotic insertion of internal oblique's and transversus abdominis's lowermost fibers, arching over the spermatic cord (or round ligament of the uterus) to attach to the pubic crest/pecten pubis, forming the posterior wall of the medial inguinal canal directly behind the superficial inguinal ring -- its integrity is central to preventing direct inguinal hernias, which characteristically occur medial to the inferior epigastric vessels through a weakness in exactly this structure (Hesselbach's triangle).
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: The shared aponeurotic insertion of internal oblique's and transversus abdominis's lower fibers, clinically central to inguinal hernia anatomy (data/fascia/trunk_fascia.json documents the related transversalis fascia/inguinal ligament structures of the same region).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
